title: Sullivan Expedition against the Haudenosaunee, 1779
summary: In 1779 a US Continental Army force under John Sullivan, joined by James Clinton's brigade, marched into Cayuga and Seneca country and burned over forty villages and at least 160,000 bushels of corn. An April raid had already struck the Onondaga capital. Survivors fled, many toward Fort Niagara, and raids resumed in 1780. Haudenosaunee people call US presidents 'Town Destroyer'.

uncertainty.note: Sources date the campaign differently: May to November 1779 overall, with the invasion of Seneca country from late August to mid-September; an earlier Onondaga raid was in April 1779. Sullivan's arrival at Tioga is given as 10 August (Encyclopedia.com) and 22 August (NPS).

importance.justification: Destroyed the Cayuga and Seneca homeland economy and became a lasting symbol of Haudenosaunee-US relations.

audience_note: Describes the deliberate burning of Haudenosaunee towns, orchards and food stores, followed by displacement, hunger and deaths among Cayuga, Seneca and Onondaga people.
